title: Proper/open interchange and its base-change and composition equations
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. Use $D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$, the bounded-below derived category of constant-coefficient module sheaves on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], derived direct images [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], and exact extension by zero along open immersions [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. For a commutative square
$$\begin{array}{ccc} A&\xrightarrow{k}&B\\ r\downarrow&&\downarrow p\\ C&\xrightarrow{i}&D\end{array}$$
with $p,r$ proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and $k,i$ open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion], there is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$\gamma_Q:i_!Rr_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_*k_!.$$
No cartesian hypothesis is imposed. Its normalization on a K-injective representative $J$ of $K\in D^+(A_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ is the morphism represented by $i_!r_*J\cong p_*k_!J\to p_*I$, where $k_!J\to I$ is a K-injective resolution [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions]; the first identification is the canonical proper/open identification of sheaves. When $A=C$, $r=\mathrm{id}$, $k=j_1$, $i=j_2$ and $p=u$ with $uj_1=j_2$, this map equals $\alpha_u$ of [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison].
For vertically stacked squares $Q_1,Q_2$ of this kind, with middle open $i_1$, bottom open $i_2$, left proper maps $r_1,r_2$, and right proper maps $p_1,p_2$, the equation is
$$\gamma_{Q_2Q_1}=(Rp_{2,*}\gamma_{Q_1})\circ(\gamma_{Q_2}Rr_{1,*}):i_{2!}Rr_{2,*}Rr_{1,*}\to Rp_{2,*}Rp_{1,*}k_{1!}.$$
For horizontally adjacent squares with left vertical $r$, middle vertical $p$, right vertical $q$, top opens $k,l$ and bottom opens $i,j$, the equation is
$$\gamma_{Q_2Q_1}=(\gamma_{Q_2}k_!)\circ(j_!\gamma_{Q_1}):j_!i_!Rr_*\to Rq_*l_!k_!,$$
All equations insert the canonical composition isomorphisms of direct images and extension by zero; squares whose two vertical maps are identities give identity comparisons, and squares whose two horizontal maps are identities give the identity on derived direct image.
Finally, let $b:D_1\to D$ be any morphism, let $Q_1$ be the base change of $Q$ by $b$, and write $a:B_1\to B$, $c:C_1\to C$, $d:A_1\to A$ for projections. Let $\beta_i:b^{-1}i_!\cong i_{1!}c^{-1}$ and $\beta_k:a^{-1}k_!\cong k_{1!}d^{-1}$ be the extension-by-zero base-change maps [cor-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change], and let $\operatorname{Ex}_r:c^{-1}Rr_*\to Rr_{1,*}d^{-1}$ and $\operatorname{Ex}_p:b^{-1}Rp_*\to Rp_{1,*}a^{-1}$ be the module exchange maps [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients]. Then
$$ (Rp_{1,*}\beta_k)\circ(\operatorname{Ex}_p k_!)\circ(b^{-1}\gamma_Q)
=(\gamma_{Q_1}d^{-1})\circ(i_{1!}\operatorname{Ex}_r)\circ(\beta_iRr_*). $$ Base changes here are formed by fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product].
